column1: Cautiously hawkish: The FOMC highlights robust job gains and low unemployment while noting “inflation remains elevated,” and pairs another 25 bp hike with ongoing QT—consistent with New Keynesian Phillips Curve logic (Gali) and Taylor-rule prescriptions when inflation is above target and slack is limited. The emphasis on “lags” and “cumulative tightening” aligns with the literature on policy transmission and narrative identification (Romer and Romer), while the move to set administered rates (IORB 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%) reflects the floor-system framework discussed by Goodfriend (2002). The warning that tighter credit will weigh on activity echoes the bank-lending/financial accelerator channel (Bernanke–Gertler) and is directionally consistent with past evidence that hawkish policy shocks tighten financial conditions (Bernanke–Mihov). The “sound and resilient” banking system and macroprudential backdrop mitigate tail risks but do not offset the near-term growth drag from higher rates and QT. Net assessment: slightly negative for growth-sensitive sentiment, supportive for inflation-control credibility. sentiment score = 0.05
